title: Constraint profile authoring and deterministic rollback policies for hybrid model rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We lack a single, authorable representation of environment constraints and rollback semantics that guarantees deterministic behavior across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Current rollout configs are fragmented (per-mode flags, ad-hoc canary schedules, env-specific heuristics) which causes surprises during promotions and inconsistent auto-rollback behavior for customers running in Private/VPC environments.

Goal: Ship a constraint-profile system plus a deterministic rollback policy DSL. Constraint profiles capture environment capabilities and limits (e.g., max-concurrent-requests, allowed-quantizations, kernel-tag availability, KV cache size, network egress policy). The rollback DSL declares triggers (latency/err/quality thresholds), confirmation windows, and remediation actions (gradual retreat, immediate rollback, traffic-fencing). The runtime will compile profiles into per-environment admission controls and a deterministic state machine used by the rollout controller so behavior is reproducible across modes.
acceptance_criteria: Constraint profile schema (JSON Schema) defined and validated with unit tests
Orchestrator can compile a profile into admission controls for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (no runtime errors)
Deterministic rollback DSL implemented with simulation mode that reproduces rollback decisions given historical telemetry
End-to-end test matrix (hosted/dedicated/private) passing for staged canaries, A/B, and shadowing with synthetic traffic
Console UI wireframe and CLI for authoring profiles available and reviewed by PM and Security
Performance regression: controller decision latency < 200ms under normal load
notes:
2025-02-14: Spike completed — validated a minimal constraint schema and a toy rollback DSL (see spike doc).
2025-02-20: POC compiled profiles into admission policies for hosted + dedicated; Private surfaced two blockers: (1) telemetry sampling is lower in air-gapped installs causing noisy metrics, (2) some private kernels are older and report different perf baselines.
Decision: add per-environment normalization steps (baseline profiling during deploy) and require a "profile-compatibility" check as part of canary initialization.
2025-02-26: Design review notes (PM + Security): require explicit KMS policy flag in profile when using model keys; disallow automatic circuit-breaker emulation when Private network isolation is detected.
2025-03-02: Infra review: we will implement deterministic rollback as a state machine persisted to the orchestrator DB so failures and restarts produce the same outcome. Rafael to own orchestration implementation; Maya to own schema and console UX.
Follow-ups: security review kickoff (sec-2025-03-05), create conformance harness for partner on-prem installs.
risk_summary: Private installs may produce false-positive rollbacks due to sparse telemetry and differing kernel baselines. Risk of customer-visible regressions if profiles are mis-authoried (e.g., enabling quantizations not supported by the node pool). Mitigations: profile-compatibility checks, mandatory dry-run simulation for Private, explicit opt-in for destructive remediation actions.
rollout_recipe_example:
# example constraint profile text (for authoring/illustration)
name: ecommerce-recommend-model-v2
environment: private
constraints:
  max_concurrent_requests: 120
  allowed_quantizations: [int8, fp16]
  kernel_tags_required: [A100-optimized, attention-fused]
  kv_cache_bytes: 2GB
  autoscaling: false
rollback_policy:
  triggers:
    - name: latency-spike
      metric: p95_latency_ms
      threshold: 1200
      window_s: 180
      confirmations: 2
      action: immediate-rollback
    - name: quality-regression
      metric: rerank_accuracy
      delta_pct: -3
      window_s: 3600
      confirmations: 3
      action: phased-retreat
notes: "when environment=private enforce profile-compatibility; require manual approval if kernel_tags_required not satisfied"
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: initial schema PR merged to repo (runtime/schema). 2025-02-24: integration tests for hosted and dedicated passing in CI. 2025-03-01: discovered telemetry sparsity; added normalization layer design. 2025-03-04: started implementing state-machine persistence and deterministic simulation harness.
review_feedback: PM (Julian Park): prefer explicit "safety-level" labels (safe, conservative, permissive) on profiles to aid non-expert operators. Design (Anya Patel): UI should expose compatibility checks and show a simulated rollout timeline before apply. Security (Liam O'Neill): must require security_review_required for any profile that allows key-material or egress to external services.
implementation_notes:
- Schema: JSON Schema + OpenAPI example; keep schema small and composable.
- Controller: compile profile into a small set of deterministic gates (resource-admission, telemetry-guard, fallback-policy).
- Simulation: feed historical traces + synthetic anomalies to the simulation harness; log decisions and diffs for audit.
- Private: profile-compatibility step runs an agent during canary initialization to snapshot node capabilities.
- Telemetry: add per-env baseline normalization (percentile mapping) to reduce false positives.
- Testing: create an isolated test fixture that mocks kernel-tag mismatches and low-sample telemetry to validate decision logic.
